Author: @FarazdakAltamimi
Comment:
The design of the experiment under discussion deliberately used a large bundle of candles in order to create the impression that the only reason for the liquid to rise was the vacuum created by the momentary cooling and contraction of the hot air, denying any role for oxygen consumption.
The denial of a vacuum due to oxygen consumption is actually due to the use of an incorrect and simplified chemical equation, which does not take into account the quantitative changes. The chemical equation must be balanced correctly. It is not true that every oxygen molecule is replaced by a carbon dioxide molecule during combustion; two oxygen molecules produce a carbon dioxide molecule and two water molecules (they condense). Recall that oxygen is present in the air as a diatomic molecule. O2 reacts with paraffin CnH2n+2. Combustion produces water H2O and carbon dioxide CO2. For n = 1, we balance the equation as follows:2 O2 + CH4 = CO2 + 2 H2OSince the amount of oxygen burned is twice the amount of carbon dioxide released, the volume of air decreases.
The claim that the temperature of hot air drops at lightning speed is unreasonable when compared to a balloon. Usually, a hot balloon can remain in the air after turning off the burner for a period ranging from 30 minutes to several hours, depending on wind factors and the ambient temperature. Newton's law of cooling states that the rate of change in the temperature of a body is proportional to the difference between its temperature and the ambient temperature.
If air pressure decreases, the temperature decreases. It also explains why air gets colder at higher altitudes, where pressure is lower. The air will not heat up and will not expand due to the occurrence of a vacuum in an upward direction and the decrease in pressure and the direct relationship between the temperature of gases and their pressure, i.e. when the pressure decreases, the temperature decreases as in the equation: T=PVnR
T=PVnR, we can decrease the temperature (T) of a gas by either decreasing its pressure (P) or its volume (V), or both.

No chemistry teacher ever should have given the "explanation" based on the oxygen being "consumed."
The same chemistry teacher should have taught the law of partial pressures.
With complete combustion of carbon, the O2 becomes CO2 -- the same number of molecules in the trapped gas and no vacuum from the oxygen being "consumed."
With incomplete combustion of carbon, the O2 becomes two molecules of CO -- more molecules in the trapped gas, which will pressurize the gas and force water out of the glass.
